member.name: T:FruityLink.Ui.Avalonia.Hosting.EmbeddedAvaloniaHost
member.summary:
Runs the Avalonia application + its IN-PROCESS on a dedicated STA thread, so a flagship Avalonia UI can be hosted inside a NON-Avalonia process (FL Studio) and reparented into FL's native host form. This is the Avalonia analog of a plugin's WPF UiHost: Avalonia and WPF coexist happily as long as each owns its own dispatcher on its own thread.
Process-singleton by necessity. Avalonia can be set up exactly ONCE per process ( / the platform threading are global). It also cannot be torn down and re-initialized cleanly, so this host owns the Avalonia thread for the WHOLE process lifetime: spins the thread + SetupWithoutStarting + a permanent once and is idempotent. Plugin enable/disable just creates/closes its window(s) on this thread — the thread keeps running so a later re-enable can reuse it.
The application is the caller's. This SDK host doesn't know the product's Application subclass: the FIRST call supplies an factory (e.g. () => AppBuilder.Configure<App>().UsePlatformDetect().WithInterFont()); the host then appends its embed-safe platform options and performs the setup on the Avalonia thread. Later calls (any overload) just wait for that one startup.
Rendering mode. As a reparented WS_CHILD of FL's non-Avalonia parent, GPU / composition presenters hit the same "airspace" problem WPF did (blank until input). We therefore pin the Win32 backend to SOFTWARE rendering onto the window's REDIRECTION SURFACE (a GDI blit), which presents reliably inside a foreign parent — the Avalonia equivalent of WPF's RenderMode.SoftwareOnly. Perf is a non-issue for a text chat.

member.name: M:FruityLink.Ui.Avalonia.Hosting.EmbeddedAvaloniaHost.EnsureStarted
member.summary: Ensure the Avalonia app + dispatcher thread is up (idempotent, once per process). Blocks the caller until Avalonia is initialized (or throws if init failed — e.g. a missing native such as libSkiaSharp, which the caller catches to fall back to another UI). Requires a previous call to have supplied the factory (); throws if none ever did.

Wraps ANY Avalonia living on the UI thread with the small Win32 glue a plugin needs to reparent it into FL's native host form and keep it painting. The plugin owns the reparent itself (the SDK's IFlWindowHost.TryEmbed takes this view's ); this class only provides the HWND, an embed-friendly / external presentation, a forced re-present (the airspace fix), and show/hide/close.
Threading. Construct + + read on the Avalonia UI thread (the plugin wraps them in ). / / self-marshal, so they are safe to call from any thread.

member.name: M:FruityLink.Ui.Avalonia.Hosting.EmbeddedAvaloniaView.ForceRender
member.summary: Force the embedded child to actually re-present. In software/redirection mode Avalonia paints via the redirection surface, but after a host hide→show (or an initial reparent) it can stay blank until an input event — so we invalidate the visual tree AND drive a synchronous native repaint. Safe from any thread.
